output_variables.consensus: All three analyses (codex __a, claude __b, lead) independently recommend against renaming sase to sawi.
output_variables.corrections:
Three source-report claims were corrected by lead verification:
1. DOMAIN ARGUMENT REVERSED: both reports treated "you own sase.sh" as a major asset to protect. Registry whois shows sawi.sh is FREE ("Domain not found") and sase.sh was created 2026-05-06 -- only ~3 months old. The .sh position is a wash, not a regression.
2. REPORT __a OVERSTATED ITS TOP FINDING: the Brazilian "SAWI OS / AI product line" is unsupported. sawi.com.br is a Campinas digital-marketing agency (est. 2008); its own about page says the name is Tupi-Guarani for "full of". No agent platform. Downgrade to moderate collision.
3. REPORT __a's FILIPINO FINDING IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE, and __b missed it entirely. Tagalog sawi = ill-fated/doomed; masawi = to die/perish; kasawian = failure. A common root, and actively bad for a reliability-oriented dev tool.
Also verified: __b's Hassan et al. provenance claim (docs/acknowledgements.md) is accurate verbatim; switching cost is 59,130 occurrences across 4,610 of 5,728 files (80%); trademark status is UNVERIFIED (__b's posture was correct, __a asserted an unconfirmable registration).
output_variables.next_step: Keep sase for now; treat the Secure Access Service Edge collision as a real but non-urgent liability. If renaming, hold candidates to the report's 8-point bar (now including a hostile-meaning check in major world languages) and decide before 1.0. Note cost is tiered: brand/code/protocol can be decoupled, so a Tier-1-only rebrand is a cheaper intermediate option.
output_variables.rationale:
Post-correction, the case against sawi rests on four points (NOT on namespaces -- sawi is clear on PyPI, crates.io, sawi-org, and sawi.sh):
1. "Structured Agentic Work Interface" is a worse expansion -- "Work" discards the most informative word for a system built on ChangeSpecs/commits/PRs, and "Interface" describes ACE alone while demoting the daemon, state store, workspace manager, and LSP.
2. The mustard pun breaks in translation: Indonesian sawi = mustard GREENS (leafy Brassica); the condiment is mustar/moster. A bottle logo needs a footnote in both languages.
3. Filipino sawi means doomed/failed -- bad for a dependability-oriented product.
4. It buys quiet, not ownership -- still hits sawi.group (cybersecurity), a squatted npm package, SAWI Academy on the .com, and it orphans ACE/AXE from the Hassan et al. lineage.
Sideways is not worth ~59,000 edits.
output_variables.salvage: The mustard-SEED metaphor is genuinely strong (smallest seed -> largest plant; one prompt -> a team of agents) but it argues for an English/botanical mustard name, not an Indonesian one. Illustrative sweep found sinapis (the botanical genus of mustard) free on PyPI, npm, .sh, and .dev.

metadata.clan_summary: [bold]RESEARCH PROMPT:[/bold] I'm thinking about renaming "sase" to "sawi" (Structured Agentic Work Interface). Can you do some research to help me decide whether this is a good idea or not? Make sure you audit existing usages of both names (i.e. look for companies or products that use the name), but also evaluate the name using your own judgement ("sawi" is also Indonesian for "mustard", but I plan on maybe using that to our advantage somehow--e.g. use a mustard bottle for our logo or something maybe). End your analysis with a recommendation on whether I should go through with this rename or not. Once you finish writing the research file, summarize its contents by setting one or more sase variables.

output_variables.research_summary: Do not rename SASE to SAWI. SASE has a severe and worsening Secure Access Service Edge search collision, so another naming round may be worthwhile before 1.0 if the product is broadening beyond software engineering. SAWI is not a strong enough destination: active adjacent users include a Brazilian AI/digital company with SAWI OS and a developer-oriented cybersecurity company; the exact npm package and obvious web domains are occupied; Filipino/Tagalog gives the spelling negative meanings; and “Work Interface” under-describes the orchestration platform. The project already owns valuable SASE assets (PyPI, sase-org, sase.sh), and a tracked six-repo census found about 68,000 SASE text occurrences across nearly 5,000 files. Keep SASE for now or seek a more distinctive, legally clearable coined name; retain the mustard idea as a mascot or release theme if desired.

output_variables.key_findings:
1. sase collision is severe: Secure Access Service Edge ($15-17B market in 2026; Zscaler, Palo Alto, Netskope, Cato, Cisco, Cloudflare, Fortinet). Adjacent industry, identical spelling, identical pronunciation ("sassy"). Search is unwinnable. Also collides with Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers (10k members).
2. The mustard pun does not survive translation: Indonesian "sawi" = mustard GREENS (leafy Brassica: sawi hijau/putih/caisim). The condiment is "mustar"/"moster". A mustard-bottle logo is a pun on the English gloss, two hops removed. It reads as a mistranslation to Indonesians and as arbitrary to everyone else.
3. Domain position REGRESSES: you own sase.sh today. For sawi, .com (Swiss SAWI Academy, est. 1968), .io, .app, .dev, .ai, .org are all taken. Only sawi.sh looks possibly free (unconfirmed). npm "sawi" is squatted.
4. sawi still collides in tech: sawi.group is a cybersecurity company - the same field being fled.
5. "Structured Agentic Work Interface" is a weaker expansion: "Work" is vaguer and less accurate than "Software Engineering"; "Interface" undersells a system with a daemon, state store, and scheduler.
6. Renaming severs the research lineage: the name comes from Hassan et al., arXiv 2509.06216, and ACE/AXE echo that paper's ACE/AEE. SAWI orphans them. (Mitigable - you can implement the SASE vision without being named after it.)
7. Niche but awkward: the Sawi people of Papua (Don Richardson's "Peace Child") are known for ritualized treachery - "fatten a victim with friendship" - an unfortunate resonance for a trustworthy-autonomous-agents product.
8. Switching cost: 58,950 occurrences across 4,599 of 5,717 tracked files, 2,712 file paths, 331 SASE_* env vars, plus PyPI, GitHub org, sase.sh, ~/.sase state dir, .sase extension, and 5 sibling repos.
output_variables.next_step: Rename is justified but needs a better candidate. Section 9 of the report lists a 7-point bar: zero enterprise-IT category collision, an actually acquirable .dev/.sh/.com, PyPI+crates+npm+Homebrew all free, unambiguous pronunciation, good CLI verb, works as a namespace, and preserves the ability to cite the SASE vision in prose. Decide while still alpha - cost only grows.
output_variables.salvage: If you like the branding hook, the mustard SEED metaphor (smallest seed -> largest plant; one prompt -> a team of agents) is legible without a footnote and botanically honest - but that argues for an English mustard-based name, not for 'sawi'.
output_variables.verdict: Do not rename sase -> sawi. The sase name IS badly broken (collides with Secure Access Service Edge, a $15-17B Gartner category, same spelling AND same pronunciation 'sassy'), but sawi is a lateral move, not an upgrade.

output_variables.caveat: Commit to the meaningful 'prompt language' reading, not last turn's opaque rhymes-with-hang framing; opacity throws away the very accuracy advantage that wins the argument
output_variables.concession: I retract the 'xprompt self-documents the relationship' claim; it names the DOMAIN correctly but models the RELATIONSHIP wrongly
output_variables.core_relationship: The true relationship is producer/product (source to output), like recipe/meal or blueprint/building; the authored artifact should NOT sound like a subtype of the thing it emits
output_variables.recommendation: Proceed to seriously prototype the rename to plang; the collision objection you waived was carrying most of my prior case, and this relationship argument dismantles the rest
output_variables.residual_xprompt_edge: xprompt still screams prompt-domain on first sight; plang costs one sentence of teaching (plang = the prompt language you author) but that is cheap
output_variables.verdict: Your critique is correct and it is the strongest argument yet; under your constraints it flips my prior recommendation from keep-xprompt toward lean-plang
output_variables.why_plang_wins: plang (read as 'prompt language') keeps the source lexically distinct from the prompt it produces, drops the false is-a, and 'language' accommodates multi-part/multi-agent/shell+python workflows better than 'prompt'
output_variables.xprompt_flaw: xprompt is a near-homophone and apparent hyponym of 'prompt', so it (a) blurs source vs runtime output and (b) falsely implies is-a-prompt, when the referent is a generator of prompts+steps
